git-staged-snapshot.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-staged-snapshot.learning_objective: Explain the working tree, index and commits, and use branches.

distractor_rationale.a: That is `git commit -a`, which stages tracked changes first.
distractor_rationale.c: Git does not refuse; it commits the staged version.
distractor_rationale.d: The working-tree edit does not replace the index until it is added again.

follow_up_questions: Which command shows the difference between the staged version and the working tree?

git-branch-is-pointer.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-branch-is-pointer.learning_objective: Explain the working tree, index and commits, and use branches.

distractor_rationale.a: Git stores snapshots once as objects; branches only point at commits.
distractor_rationale.b: No archive is made; existing objects are reused.
distractor_rationale.c: Creating a branch makes no commit.

follow_up_questions: What happens to the `feature` pointer when you commit on it?

git-amend-unpushed.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-amend-unpushed.learning_objective: Explain the working tree, index and commits, and use branches.

distractor_rationale.a: Revert adds an undo commit; the typo stays in history.
distractor_rationale.d: `--hard` discards the commit's changes from the working tree.

follow_up_questions: Why would amending be a problem if the commit were already on a shared branch?

git-fast-forward.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-fast-forward.learning_objective: Choose between merge and rebase and resolve conflicts safely.

distractor_rationale.b: Happens only when both sides diverged, or with --no-ff.

follow_up_questions: Why do some teams require `--no-ff` merges?

git-ignore-tracked-file.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-ignore-tracked-file.learning_objective: Choose between merge and rebase and resolve conflicts safely.

distractor_rationale.a: Ignore rules take effect immediately in the working tree.
distractor_rationale.b: A pattern with a slash in the middle already matches relative to the .gitignore location.
distractor_rationale.d: Git reads the working-tree .gitignore even before it is committed.

follow_up_questions: The file contained a database password. What else must you do?

git-revert-shared.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-revert-shared.learning_objective: Choose between merge and rebase and resolve conflicts safely.

distractor_rationale.a: Rewrites shared history that others have pulled.
distractor_rationale.c: Amend rewrites the last commit and needs a force push too.
distractor_rationale.d: Also rewrites shared history, and may lose others' commits.

follow_up_questions: How do you revert a merge commit, and what does `-m 1` mean?

git-reflog-recover.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-reflog-recover.learning_objective: Recover lost work and rewrite history without harming collaborators.

distractor_rationale.a: The objects stay until garbage collection prunes unreachable ones.
distractor_rationale.c: Revert creates inverse commits; it cannot restore discarded commits.
distractor_rationale.d: fsck can list dangling commits but does not move branches; the reflog is the direct route.

follow_up_questions: Uncommitted changes were also discarded by the reset. Can the reflog recover them? Why not?

git-force-with-lease.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-force-with-lease.learning_objective: Recover lost work and rewrite history without harming collaborators.

distractor_rationale.a: Silently discards any commit pushed since your last fetch.
distractor_rationale.b: Pushes never merge; the push is rejected as non-fast-forward.
distractor_rationale.d: Same effect as --force, and closes the pull request on some hosts.

follow_up_questions: Why can an IDE that fetches in the background make `--force-with-lease` unsafe?

git-hash-chain.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-hash-chain.learning_objective: Recover lost work and rewrite history without harming collaborators.

distractor_rationale.b: Messages are unchanged; the committer date does change, but the parent chain alone forces new hashes.
distractor_rationale.c: Tree objects can be identical; the parent field still differs.

follow_up_questions: Why does this property make signed tags meaningful?

git-force-pushed-main.provenance: ai-assisted draft (Claude), self-reviewed, blind second-model review; pending independent human review
git-force-pushed-main.learning_objective: Recover lost work and rewrite history without harming collaborators.
